title: SwiftSpec: Ultra-Low Latency LLM Decoding by Scaling Asynchronous Speculative Decoding
quote: redesigns the speculative decoding pipeline in an asynchronous and disaggregated manner
proves: Draft and target on separate GPU groups within one node; 1.75x over SOTA SD on average; Llama3-70B at 348 tok/s on 8 Hopper GPUs.
does_not_prove: Single node, NVLink; latency-focused, not throughput serving; no cross-node or shared-drafter results.
bearing: Anchor: draft-on-separate-GPU is answered for batch-1 latency in one node.

title: SwiftSpec (HTML full text): GPU partition, data exchanged, batch limits
quote: We partition GPUs into two groups: verification and draft.
proves: Split chosen by profiling (e.g. 2 draft + 6 target GPUs, often 4+4); only draft-tree tokens and verified tokens cross groups, draft keeps its own KV; batch sizes kept small (<=16); int4 kernels not suitable for batch 64+.
does_not_prove: No measured cost of the draft-target link; no statement on high-batch serving or cross-node placement.
bearing: Supports gap: disaggregated drafting at serving batch sizes and across nodes is untested in SwiftSpec.

title: PipeSpec: Breaking Stage Dependencies in Hierarchical LLM Decoding
venue: arXiv preprint (abstract page lists no venue)
quote: providing a scalable approach to accelerating LLM inference on multi-device systems
proves: Chain of k models, each on its own device, async producer-consumer with rollback; up to 2.54x speedup.
does_not_prove: Single-request latency; no multi-tenant serving, no network cost study.
bearing: Anchor for multi-device draft pipelines; threatens novelty of plain async multi-GPU drafting.

title: AMUSD: Asynchronous Multi-Device Speculative Decoding for LLM Acceleration
quote: AMUSD enables both models to perform predictions independently on separate devices (e.g., GPUs).
proves: Draft and verify on separate GPUs concurrently; average 29% over SD, up to 1.96x over autoregressive.
does_not_prove: Batch 1 only; extra GPU cost not normalized.
bearing: Anchor; same as A3.

title: Distributed Speculative Inference (DSI): Speculation Parallelism for Provably Faster Lossless Language Model Inference
quote: DSI is 1.29-1.92x faster than SI in single-node setups
proves: Speculation parallelism orchestrates overlapping target and drafter instances; provably faster than SI and non-SI for any drafter; 1.29-1.92x over SI.
does_not_prove: Numbers are simulations; no serving system, no GPU-cost or batch analysis.
bearing: Theoretical anchor for multi-instance drafting; does not cover shared resources.

title: PEARL: Parallel Speculative Decoding with Adaptive Draft Length
quote: the target model gets stuck when the draft model is guessing tokens, and vice versa
proves: Pre-verify and post-verify remove mutual waiting; up to 4.43x over AR and 1.50x over vanilla SD.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not state device placement; batch-1 focus.
bearing: Anchor parallel SD; later papers (A20) use a dedicated draft GPU for PEARL.

title: Speculative Speculative Decoding (Saguaro)
quote: Unlike ordinary speculative decoding, in SSD the draft model is located on distinct hardware from the target.
proves: Target on 4xH100 TP=4, draft on separate 1xH100; draft precomputes a speculation cache for likely verify outcomes; ~30% over optimized SD, up to 5x over AR; more speculation devices give larger caches.
does_not_prove: Paper itself says SD is generally ineffective for throughput-bound workloads, cache misses stall the whole batch at large batch, and returns from more draft GPUs diminish; no dollar/utilization cost.
bearing: Strong prior art for dedicated draft GPU; its stated large-batch limit is an opening.

title: SpecEdge: Scalable Edge-Assisted Serving Framework for Interactive LLMs
quote: exchanging only token outputs over the network
proves: Edge GPU drafts, server verifies; proactive edge drafting overlaps with verification; pipeline-aware scheduling interleaves users; 1.91x cost efficiency, 2.22x server throughput, 11.24% lower ITL.
does_not_prove: Assumes consumer GPU at the edge; WAN variability and drafter failure not the focus.
bearing: Anchor for edge-cloud drafting and multi-user server-side pipelining.

title: Speculation at a Distance: Where Edge-Cloud Speculative Decoding Actually Pays Off
quote: Pipelining can make DSD competitive with co-located SD only in low-RTT regimes.
proves: Closed-form: if the server can host both models, co-located SD beats synchronous distributed SD in latency and communication; at WAN RTT pipelined DSD still loses; DSD's case is multi-tenant capacity, about (1 + gamma*t_d/t_v)x more clients.
does_not_prove: No numeric RTT threshold or measured system; datacenter (RDMA/NVLink) RTTs not studied.
bearing: Negative evidence: kills remote drafting for latency; leaves capacity framing open.

title: FlexSpec: Frozen Drafts Meet Evolving Targets in Edge-Cloud Collaborative LLM Speculative Decoding
quote: existing frameworks fundamentally rely on tight coupling between the two models
proves: One static edge draft serves many evolving cloud targets via shared backbone; channel-aware draft length.
does_not_prove: No numbers on the abstract page.
bearing: Touches drafter-shared-across-targets, but for model versions, not GPU sharing.

title: Quantize-Sample-and-Verify: LLM Acceleration via Adaptive Edge-Cloud Speculative Decoding
quote: A key bottleneck in such systems is the limited communication bandwidth between edge and cloud.
proves: Quantizes what the edge sends while provably preserving the cloud distribution; adapts draft length and precision to channel.
does_not_prove: Simulation only, no numbers in abstract.
bearing: Communication cost of draft payloads is treated only for edge links.

title: Dovetail: A CPU/GPU Heterogeneous Speculative Decoding for LLM inference
quote: Dovetail deploys a draft model on the GPU
proves: Draft on GPU, target on CPU for memory-limited machines; 1.79x-10.1x on 13B models.
does_not_prove: Single user, consumer hardware.
bearing: Heterogeneous placement covered for local inference.

title: DuoDecoding: Hardware-aware Heterogeneous Speculative Decoding with Dynamic Multi-Sequence Drafting
quote: strategically deploys the draft and target models on the CPU and GPU respectively
proves: CPU drafter in parallel with GPU target; up to 2.61x latency speedup; TTFT 83% of conventional SD.
does_not_prove: Batch 1; no serving.
bearing: Covers CPU drafting on one box; relevant to Mac unified memory.

title: Mirror Speculative Decoding: Breaking the Serial Barrier in LLM Inference
quote: explicitly maps computation across heterogeneous accelerators (GPU and NPU) to exploit cross-device parallelism
proves: GPU+NPU split with bidirectional speculation; 2.8x-5.8x wall-time on SpecBench for 14B-66B; ~30% over EAGLE3.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not say which device runs which model; batch-1 latency.
bearing: NPU drafting is taken; threatens Apple-ANE drafting novelty.

title: HeteroReason: Heterogeneous FPGA-GPU Acceleration for Disaggregated Speculative Reasoning
quote: the draft model is offloaded to the FPGA while deploying the PRM and target models on GPUs
proves: Draft on FPGA, target and PRM on GPUs, with PD disaggregation and shadow sync; 1.01x-1.42x latency, 1.25x-1.57x energy.
does_not_prove: Draft-KV movement not described on abstract page; small latency gains.
bearing: Heterogeneous drafting in reasoning; modest gains suggest limited headroom.

title: [RFC]: Disaggregated Speculative Decoding with Standalone Parallel Draft Model (vLLM #42109)
quote: N verify servers can share M draft servers
proves: Proposed N:M verify:draft topology with DraftRouter; wire = verify outcome (k_accepted, bonus token, temps) and K draft tokens, no hidden states; POC 3:2 claims ~1.4x TPOT vs co-located at same GPU budget; a user reports cross-node spec slower than no-spec and below in-model MTP; notes vLLM lacks an API to score externally drafted tokens.
does_not_prove: Open, no maintainer comments, no upstream PR; POC data not published; EAGLE/MTP (hidden-state drafters) excluded.
bearing: Directly on shared drafter pool; open question for hidden-state drafters and router policy.

title: [Feature][RFC] SPECTRE: Parallel Speculative Decoding with a Multi-Tenant Remote Drafter (SGLang #22044)
quote: Instead of dedicating an underutilized GPU solely to the Drafter, SPECTRE treats it as a multi-tenant service.
proves: Drafter serves its own users plus remote draft requests in one batch over ZMQ; mixed mode has no strong isolation; circuit breaker falls back to AR; Qwen3-32B/0.6B: 1.76x dedicated, 1.74x mixed while drafter's own throughput drops to 0.87x.
does_not_prove: Closed by inactivity bot, not merged; one model pair; no SLO study of the tenant trade-off.
bearing: Strongly on drafter-as-shared-service and isolation; leaves policy/isolation open.

title: NebulaSD: Many-for-Many Speculative Decoding
quote: independently schedulable resource pools
proves: Draft and target workers in separate pools with shared request pools and migration-aware async KV prep; +50.4% over fixed-pair disaggregated and +72.6% over co-located on 4 GPUs.
does_not_prove: Metric is request-round rate on 4 GPUs; abstract silent on tenants, heterogeneity, comm cost; scaling only simulated under idealized state movement.
bearing: Threatens drafter-pool / elastic draft capacity ideas directly (last 30 days).

title: Resource-Efficient Speculative Decoding for Long-Context LLM Serving (SpecStream)
quote: faster drafting need not shorten a round dominated by historical KV reads
proves: Same-GPU drafting gets 1.036x the throughput of SPECTRE+Offload with a dedicated third draft GPU, i.e. 55.4% more per GPU; separate GPUs must exchange candidates and verification results.
does_not_prove: Only for long-context, KV-offload-bound setup; 2 vs 3 GPU config.
bearing: Negative evidence for dedicated draft GPUs when target is KV-bound.

title: When Parallel Drafter Meets Parallel Speculative Decoding (DPara)
quote: retains 90%-95% of DPara's speedup across batch sizes 1-4 while halving the GPU count
proves: PEARL, SSD and DPara all use one extra dedicated drafting GPU; colocated DPara-single keeps 90-95% of speedup at batch 1-4 with half the GPUs, but the advantage disappears at batch 8 and 16; dedicated drafting preferable as batch grows.
does_not_prove: H800 single node; dense Qwen3 8B/14B; no network separation.
bearing: Mixed: colocation wins at small batch, separation at larger batch; crossover depends on hardware.

title: SpecBranch: Speculative Decoding via Hybrid Drafting and Rollback-Aware Branch Parallelism
quote: the key challenge lies in the trade-offs between parallelization and token rollback
proves: Parallel branches hedge rejections; 1.8x-4.5x over AR; rollback tokens -50% for poorly aligned pairs.
does_not_prove: Multi-pair sharing only sketched.
bearing: Rollback waste is the cost of async drafting on separate devices.

title: EasySpec: Layer-Parallel Speculative Decoding for Efficient Multi-GPU Utilization
quote: the optimal TP size of the draft model is typically smaller than that of the base model
proves: Under TP, GPUs idle during drafting; layer-parallel draft gives up to 1.62x faster drafting, 4.17x peak over vanilla.
does_not_prove: Colocated multi-GPU only.
bearing: Quantifies idle GPUs during drafting, a motive for disaggregation.

title: MineDraft: A Framework for Batch Parallel Speculative Decoding
quote: maintains two batches of requests, overlapping drafting for one batch with verification for the other
proves: Two-batch ping-pong drafting/verification; up to 75% throughput, 39% lower end-to-end latency.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not state hardware placement.
bearing: Batch-level overlap already explored; threatens ping-pong ideas.

title: Dynamo Known Issues (v1.3.0: Disagg Decode + EAGLE3 Speculative Decoding Crashes Silently)
quote: EAGLE3 speculative decoding with disaggregated serving is unsupported.
proves: In Dynamo v1.3.0 (vLLM backend) EAGLE3 under PD crashes under large KV-transfer volume, fix targeted v1.4.0; planner's MTP accept length pins at 1.0 so autoscaling ignores it.
does_not_prove: Bug-level; no perf data.
bearing: PD+spec is immature in production; planner ignores speculation in capacity decisions.

title: Speculative Decoding with SGLang (Dynamo docs)
quote: Speculation runs on the decode worker, so read its metrics on port 8082.
proves: Disaggregated EAGLE3 recipe: same spec flags on prefill and decode workers, NIXL transfer, drafting on decode worker; only EAGLE3 validated end to end.
does_not_prove: No placement alternatives or numbers.
bearing: Production default: draft colocated with decode worker.

title: Accelerating SGLang with Multiple Token Prediction (LMSYS blog)
quote: now supports smooth combination of these advanced features
proves: MTP + large EP + PD in SGLang; 16xH200 decode: 51.0 -> 82.0 tok/s/rank (accept length 2.44); 128 H200 (4P/12D) at 128 req/rank: +14.2%.
does_not_prove: Does not state where draft runs or how draft state moves P->D.
bearing: Shows MTP gains shrink at large batch in PD (60% -> 14%).

title: [Bug]: Gemma 4 MTP + NIXL PD disaggregation - draft model KV not transferred, MTP ineffective (vLLM #54926)
quote: the draft model's KV state built during prefill is never transferred to the decode pod
proves: Draft KV skipped by NIXL, so decode re-runs MTP from scratch, wiping MTP benefit at ISL 15k.
does_not_prove: Open, no fix, no acceptance numbers.
bearing: Draft-state transfer in PD is an open engineering gap.

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Preserve EAGLE/MTP draft KV during CPU retraction (SGLang PR 44899)
quote: Missing draft history can reduce speculative acceptance; target verification still runs.
proves: Separate EAGLE/MTP pools were not included in retraction backup; fix verified byte-identical on 4 ranks (GLM-5.3, 131063 positions).
does_not_prove: No throughput claim; open PR.
bearing: Draft state is second-class in PD memory management.

title: fix(dflash): reject unsupported PD disaggregation (SGLang PR 36277)
quote: transfers target KV state and EAGLE-style final hidden state, but not DFLASH's per-layer draft state
proves: SGLang PD wire carries target KV + EAGLE final hidden state only; DFlash per-layer draft state is not transferred, so PD+DFlash crashes/hangs; PR only fails fast.
does_not_prove: No support added; open PR.
bearing: Opening: per-drafter state transfer cost/protocol in PD is unsolved for newer drafters.

title: DSpark speculative decoding incompatible with NIXL P/D disaggregation and Hopper FA3 (vLLM #48221)
quote: AssertionError: Number of KV layers must match between producer and consumer
proves: Draft-only-on-decode adds extra KV layers and breaks NIXL handshake; workaround is drafting on both sides, which wastes prefill memory.
does_not_prove: Open; FA3 crash partially fixed.
bearing: Draft placement asymmetry between P and D is not supported.

title: [Roadmap]: PD Disaggregation with NixlConnector Roadmap (vLLM #33702)
quote: P/D disaggregation with speculative decoding +CI
proves: PD+SD integration is WIP; asymmetric num_speculative_tokens needs roles at config time; prefix-cache trimming bug with lookahead block; maintainer suspected draft-layer KV not saved/loaded properly.
does_not_prove: Roadmap, no perf data.
bearing: Confirms production PD+spec is immature as of Oct 2026.

title: Disaggregated Inference design (AWS Neuron vLLM)
quote: runs spec decoding to generate the draft KV cache
proves: Neuron DI runs Eagle3 on prefill to build draft KV and ships both target and draft KV to decode; tested with DP+EP topologies.
does_not_prove: Page is internally inconsistent (table says draft on decode side); no cost numbers.
bearing: One production answer to draft-KV placement in PD.

title: MegaScale-Infer: Serving Mixture-of-Experts at Scale with Disaggregated Expert Parallelism
quote: MegaScale-Infer disaggregates attention and FFN modules within each model layer, enabling independent scaling,
proves: AFD with ping-pong micro-batch pipeline; up to 1.90x per-GPU throughput.
does_not_prove: Read portion has no mention of speculative decoding or MTP.
bearing: Gap: speculation (verify widens tokens per step) under AFD unstudied.

title: Step-3 is Large yet Affordable: Model-system Co-design for Cost-effective Decoding
quote: (4K context, FP8, no MTP)
proves: AFD decode at 4,039 tok/s/GPU under 50 ms TPOT, explicitly without MTP.
does_not_prove: No speculation results under AFD.
bearing: Supports gap: AFD + MTP/spec unmeasured.

title: Revealing the Challenges of Attention-FFN Disaggregation for Modern MoE Models and Hardware Systems
quote: Our analysis reveals a dead zone on standard clusters
proves: AFD has a dead zone on standard clusters where adding FFN instances fails to raise utilization due to scale-out bandwidth.
does_not_prove: No speculation/MTP analysis on page.
bearing: Spec raises tokens/step, which could move AFD out of the dead zone; untested.

title: Frontier: Towards Comprehensive and Accurate LLM Inference Simulation
quote: the verify phase is a prefill-like forward pass that can share a batch with ordinary decode work
proves: Simulator models MTP (per-request accept state) and AFD/PDD separately; validated MTP fidelity mostly <10% error.
does_not_prove: No result on MTP combined with AFD or PDD.
bearing: Tool for studying spec x AFD; gap confirmed.

title: When Does Disaggregation Pay? Simulating Prefill--Decode--Attention--FFN Specialization for Agentic LLM Inference
quote: 4 way Prefill Decode Attention FFN disaggregation is the most consistent for increasing throughput
proves: Simulated PD gives up to 75% throughput; 4-way PDAF most consistent, assuming custom NPUs.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not mention speculation.
bearing: Spec missing from disaggregation design-space studies.

title: StreamServe: Adaptive Speculative Flows for Low-Latency Disaggregated LLM Serving
quote: jointly adapting routing and speculation within a disaggregated framework
proves: Routing + online speculation depth in a disaggregated setup; 11-18x lower latency than TP vLLM; 4xA800 as two stream pairs.
does_not_prove: Small testbed, 320 queries; baseline is TP not PD+spec.
bearing: Partially covers spec inside disaggregated serving.

title: SpecForge v0.3.0: a Unified Disaggregated and Colocated Speculative Decoding Stack (LMSYS)
quote: Captured hidden states can be large, so forwarding them through a Python queue or control database would quickly become a bottleneck
proves: Draft training disaggregated from target capture via Mooncake; ~10% training throughput over colocated on 8xH20.
does_not_prove: Training only, not serving.
bearing: Hidden-state transport over Mooncake exists for training; serving analog open.

title: Extracting hidden states from vLLM
quote: this adds up to 268 MB of data
proves: Qwen3-8B, 8k tokens, 4 layers FP16 hidden states = 268 MB; moved via KV Connector (the PD machinery).
does_not_prove: Prefill-time capture for training; per-decode-step hidden-state size/latency not given.
bearing: Gives a number for hidden-state transfer cost; EAGLE remote drafting would pay this.

title: How speculative decoding supercharged AI inference in disaggregated pipelines (d-Matrix)
quote: GPUs excel at pre-fill
proves: Vendor pitch: draft on memory-optimized accelerator, target on GPU.
does_not_prove: No numbers; marketing.
bearing: Industry interest in heterogeneous draft placement.

title: Disaggregated Speculative Decoding and Fused Kernels (SwiftSpec, ACM)
proves: Not verified: fetch returned HTTP 403.
does_not_prove: Venue and content unconfirmed.
bearing: Same as A1.

title: vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py (main)
quote: Allocate speculative lookahead slots later to avoid mismatching local and remote block counts. / We don't schedule partial draft tokens since this prevents uniform decode optimizations. / Prefer to not schedule than schedule un-padded.
proves: vLLM V1 calls allocate_slots(request, num_new_tokens, num_lookahead_tokens=self.num_lookahead_tokens) inside schedule(), before the forward pass, for every running request; waiting requests get the same lookahead unless they have an async KV load. num_new_tokens comes from num_tokens_with_spec, so draft tokens consume token_budget; drafts are scheduled all-or-nothing and new decode requests are padded to 1+num_spec_tokens to keep full CUDA graphs. On allocation failure the scheduler preempts running[-1] (or lowest priority) and frees all its blocks; a step that preempts admits no waiting requests.
does_not_prove: Does not show how many blocks the lookahead actually adds per request (at most one block per request when K < block_size) or how often lookahead causes a preemption that a non-spec run would not have. No measurement.
bearing: Supports any idea about lazy/elastic lookahead reservation or spec-aware admission; shows the reservation is static per step and preemption is all-or-nothing.

title: vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py (main)
quote: num_lookahead_tokens: The number of speculative tokens to allocate. This is used by spec decode proposers with kv-cache such as eagle.
proves: allocate_slots sizes the request to min(num_tokens_main_model + num_lookahead_tokens, max_model_len) and allocates blocks for new + lookahead tokens; only verified tokens are cached (capped at request.num_tokens). No code in allocate_slots frees lookahead blocks after rejection; rejected-token rollback is mentioned only for skipped-block freeing.
does_not_prove: Does not quantify waste; lookahead blocks are reused next step by the same request, so the cost is a transient per-request block, not a leak.
bearing: Bounds the size of the reservation waste (sub-block per request); threatens ideas that assume large lookahead waste in vLLM chain drafting.

title: [Performance]: Dynamic speculative decoding (num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size) causes catastrophic aggregate-throughput collapse under concurrency at the batch-size threshold (MTP, V1/PIECEWISE) (vLLM issue 49548)
quote: Reserved lookahead slots are normally transient, but they still count against the free-block admission check
proves: With dynamic K, num_lookahead_tokens stays fixed at the static num_spec_tokens, so lookahead is reserved even when the per-batch K is 0. Reporter saw 8 concurrent x 180 tokens drop from ~232 tok/s aggregate to 24-157 tok/s (Qwen3.5-122B MTP k=2, GB10).
does_not_prove: The lookahead hypothesis is the author's lowest-confidence one and was never tested; follow-up PR 51466 found no throughput gain and was closed. Collapse is more likely CUDA-graph dispatch related. Open, no maintainer reply.
bearing: Open question: whether reservation should track the dynamic K. Weak support for a reservation-sizing idea; strong warning that the collapse cause is unconfirmed.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Fix speculative block reservations across KV cache groups (vLLM PR 59880)
quote: under-reserving these blocks can leave a request admitted for an asynchronous KV load but unable to start decoding
proves: vLLM already reserves spec-decode blocks at admission for async KV loads (reserved_blocks); before this fix (merged 2026-10-11) the reservation was under-counted for multi-group / hybrid models. Fix sums reservation per cache manager by block size; in-flight lookahead accounting moved into cache managers; Mamba excluded from admission margin.
does_not_prove: Correctness fix with tests only; no capacity or throughput numbers. Reviewer estimate of ~1 block per Mamba group over-reserve is not measured.
bearing: Shows spec-aware admission reservation exists in vLLM now; threatens 'nobody accounts for speculative reservations at admission'.

title: [P/D][Bugfix] Fix PD async KV load lookahead handling for MTP spec decode (vLLM PR 46694)
quote: Fix NIXL async KV load handling for speculative decoding by deferring lookahead slot allocation during remote KV receive.
proves: Merged 2026-07-09: lookahead slots are deferred while a request receives remote KV in P/D, because eager lookahead made local and remote block counts disagree.
does_not_prove: Deferral is limited to the P/D receive step, not a general lazy-reservation policy; no memory numbers.
bearing: Shows deferral of lookahead is already practiced in one path; partial threat to a 'deferred lookahead' idea, support for generalizing it.

title: [Bug]: [PD + SpecDec] Prefix-cache trimming drops wrong block when P has extra lookahead block (vLLM issue 43996)
quote: P keeps its full num_lookahead_tokens, so at block boundaries P allocates one more block than D.
proves: Lookahead reservation on the prefill node (which never decodes) creates an extra block at block boundaries and a wrong-block transfer bug.
does_not_prove: Closed as not planned (stale); correctness only, no capacity cost measured.
bearing: Evidence that lookahead reservation is applied where it is useless (prefill role); supports role-aware reservation ideas.

title: [Bugfix][Core][Spec Decode] Skip spec-decode block reservation on the external-KV-load step (P/D) (vLLM PR 50173)
quote: the decode over-allocates KV blocks on a request's initial external-KV-load step
proves: Both the lookahead reservation and pad_spec_decode over-allocate on the first decode step after KV transfer: DeepSeek-R1 TP8 1P1D MTP1 block_size=64, 959-token prompt: P sent 15 blocks, D reserved 16, crashing on assert; fix gives 512/512 gsm8k completions.
does_not_prove: Open, not merged, needs rebase. Harm is a crash, not capacity; one surplus block per request.
bearing: Shows reservation semantics still being patched case by case (Jul-Oct 2026); weak support for a principled reservation model.

title: [Core] Avoid mixed batch on spec-dec D-node via padding (vLLM PR 45237)
quote: This PR lets the decode-side scheduler optionally pad the first post-transfer step with dummy speculative tokens
proves: Padding a newly transferred request to 1+N dummy spec tokens keeps the batch on the full CUDA graph. GLM-5.1 NVFP4 8xB300: mean TPOT 38.83 ms padding off vs 16.99 ms on; CUDA graph launches 44 to 1. Padding is coordinated across DP ranks.
does_not_prove: Single-run numbers; the dummy-token padding also costs KV slots and compute that the PR does not measure.
bearing: Shows deliberate over-reservation (padding) is a net win for latency; threatens ideas that treat padding as pure waste.

title: [RFC]: Automate Speculative Decoding (vLLM issue 4565)
quote: For instance, if num_lookahead_slots is set to 5 but the proposed length is only 3, then 2 slots would go unused.
proves: The vLLM spec-decode authors named the static lookahead-slot reservation vs dynamic proposal length as a memory inefficiency in 2024.
does_not_prove: Closed as not planned (stale, 2025); V0-era; no measurement of the waste.
bearing: Shows the over-reservation gap was known and never quantified or fixed; supports a measurement-first candidate.

title: [RFC]: Sparse-attention-based self-speculative decoding (StreamingLLM, then Vegas) (vLLM issue 47351)
quote: Reserves lookahead slots so KV pages are allocated for draft tokens
proves: New proposers (self-speculation) plan to reuse the same lookahead-slot reservation mechanism.
does_not_prove: No memory analysis; RFC is stale.
bearing: Weak: shows lookahead reservation is the default design for new proposers.

title: Spec v2 tree drafting (topk>1) with page_size>1 (SGLang PR 26972)
quote: the draft reserves a page-aligned per-branch footprint of `2 * get_alloc_len_per_decode`
proves: SGLang tree drafting with topk>1 and page_size>1 reserves 2 x (topk x num_new_pages x page_size) slots per request per decode; before the fix (merged 2026-06-06) over-allocated slots were never freed (pool leak) and indexing overflowed. Row widened to max(4 + num_draft_tokens, 2*alloc_len).
does_not_prove: No numbers on how much KV the page-aligned tree reservation costs at batch scale.
bearing: Strong support: tree speculation with paging multiplies reservation by topk x page_size; a measurable over-reservation gap.

title: [Bug] Prefill out of memory during eagle_worker verify (SGLang issue 13765)
quote: compute an appropriate KV cache buffer size for the speculative decoding process of each request
proves: SGLang EAGLE verify failed allocating 508 tokens with 448 available when the pool was full; reporter proposed a per-request reserved speculative KV buffer accounted for by the scheduler. Others reported similar retractions.
does_not_prove: No maintainer reply; auto-closed as inactive; reporter's diagnosis unconfirmed.
bearing: Supports 'spec KV is not reserved at admission in SGLang, so verify can OOM at high load'.

title: [Bug][Speculative] EAGLE/MTP causes 90% KV cache starvation on models with untied embeddings (Fix Included) (SGLang issue 44145)
quote: this locks out over 90% of the KV cache capacity permanently
proves: Single GPU: KV pool 225,211 tokens without spec, 15,363 with stock EAGLE MTP, 169,603 with patch (draft embedding/LM head counted before sharing). Opened 2026-10-13, fix PR 45151 open.
does_not_prove: A memory-profiling bug for one model class, not an inherent cost of speculation; even patched, capacity drops 25%.
bearing: Strong evidence spec decode can silently cost large batch capacity; supports measurement of capacity cost per method.

title: Speculative Decoding (SGLang docs)
quote: These three parameters directly control how much memory the draft tree consumes
proves: SGLang docs: steps, topk and num_draft_tokens set draft-tree memory; spec decode may increase memory via draft tree, CUDA graphs and verification buffers; OOM advice is lower mem-fraction-static, cuda-graph-max-bs, tree size, or limit concurrency. Overlap scheduler supports only topk 1.
does_not_prove: No numbers; guidance is manual static tuning.
bearing: Supports 'reservation for speculation is set by hand, not by load'; candidate for automatic sizing.

title: tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/resource_manager.py (main)
quote: Dynamic-tree draft manager reserves K*max_draft_len KV slots (the draft loop can write that many even if max_total_draft_tokens is smaller).
proves: TRT-LLM admission budget per request is blocks to completion for prompt + max_new_tokens + num_extra_kv_tokens + _kv_reserve_draft_tokens; each generation step adds 1 + max(draft_len, reserve) tokens, then rewinds rejected tokens (rewind_kv_cache). Dynamic-tree drafter reserves topK x max_draft_len slots.
does_not_prove: Source read only; no measurement of capacity lost. Fetched via curl, not WebFetch.
bearing: Shows a production engine reserves worst-case draft KV at admission (strict, mode-2-like); supports comparing strict vs optimistic reservation.

title: speculative decoding (vllm-metal docs)
quote: Its committed KV and speculative lookahead share the Metal KV memory budget with the target.
proves: On vllm-metal (user's hardware), draft_model uses a second scheduler-managed KV cache; MTP reads target KV; n-gram has no extra KV. The scheduler allocates both, no separate draft scratch pool. Experimental DFlash and DSpark use scheduler-owned cache lifecycle.
does_not_prove: Gives no sizes; the 'un-budgeted KV cache' phrase in an earlier search snippet was not on the page.
bearing: Makes a reservation experiment feasible on the M5: lookahead and draft KV come out of one budget the scheduler controls.

title: Adaptive Verification in vLLM: DSpark confidence-scheduled verification (blog)
quote: Inside the captured CUDA graphs cost is a staircase rather than a line, because of cudagraph padding
proves: A 121-token batch pays for the 128-token graph; budget B is chosen to maximize expected tokens per step time using load; slots compete across requests. Larger capture size needs more cudagraph memory, so the repro uses --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 because it OOMs at default.
does_not_prove: Says nothing about KV slots for drafted vs verified tokens; memory cost of graphs not quantified.
bearing: Shows verification compute is already allocated across requests by load (threat to verify-budget ideas); hints CUDA-graph memory is a hidden reservation cost.

title: Resource-Efficient Speculative Decoding for Long-Context LLM Serving (SpecStream)
quote: GPU memory limits force additional requests to queue, causing AR and SGLang SD throughput to saturate.
proves: SpecStream keeps the full draft KV on GPU, which takes a growing share of memory with concurrency; offloads committed history to CPU (starts at 8 concurrent on Qwen3); keeps unverified candidates on GPU so rejections need no cross-device cleanup; 1.41x/1.32x over TriForce.
does_not_prove: Long-context, offloading setting; does not isolate the cost of speculative reservation vs draft KV history.
bearing: Shows draft KV share under concurrency is a recognized cost; commit-aware tiering is taken.

title: Nightjar: Dynamic Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Large Language Models Serving
quote: Under high request load, the memory occupied by these draft models directly competes with the KV cache.
proves: Nightjar disables SD under load and offloads the draft model to CPU when free KV blocks stay below a threshold; reload needs an empty queue and free blocks. SD degrades throughput up to 30.25% vs no-SD at high load; Nightjar up to 14.76% over standard SD.
does_not_prove: Reclaims draft weights, not lookahead/draft-KV reservations; 7B/13B scale.
bearing: Threatens 'reclaim speculative memory under pressure' ideas: draft-weight reclaim is done.

title: Speculative Decoding: Performance or Illusion?
quote: We find that the memory overhead of speculative decoding (SD) is minimal.
proves: Per-token KV: Llama3-70B 320 KiB target-only vs 352 KiB with 1B draft; Qwen3-8B 144 to 256 KiB with 0.6B draft. Reasoning workloads can trigger preemption once KV fills, so experiments were kept to medium batch.
does_not_prove: Does not measure maximum batch size or preemption rate with vs without SD.
bearing: Negative result for memory-cost ideas: authors call overhead minimal, but the Qwen3-8B 78% per-token increase and untested max batch leave the capacity question open.

title: Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context
quote: bounds the draft's KV working set to a constant
proves: Unread draft KV is 7.7-11% of total KV at 1M context; sliding window + sink on draft attention drops ~99% of draft KV entries, reclaimed via a ring buffer.
does_not_prove: Million-token regime; single author; abstract only.
bearing: Threat: shrinking draft-KV footprint is being done for MTP.

title: H-Spec: Parallel Speculative Decoding Without a Drafter-Side KV Cache
quote: add per-request memory and KV-write overhead that grow with concurrency
proves: Block drafters (DFlash-style) keep a separate drafter-side KV cache whose memory grows with concurrency; H-Spec removes it and reports lower KV utilization across concurrency levels.
does_not_prove: Abstract gives no absolute memory or concurrency numbers.
bearing: Threat: drafter-KV elimination is recent and active (Sep 2026).

title: Efficient Speculative Decoding for Llama at Scale: Challenges and Solutions
quote: we add additional tree padding when allocating blocks for drafting and validation stages
proves: Meta production EAGLE: paged KV is not compatible with tree attention, so paging applies to the prefix only; separate base and draft caches; extra tree padding is reserved per block allocation so speculative tokens never cross block boundaries.
does_not_prove: Does not quantify the padding's memory cost or its effect on batch capacity.
bearing: Supports: production systems over-reserve for tree speculation; cost unmeasured.

title: SpecMemo: Speculative Decoding is in Your Pocket
quote: Speculative decoding pre-allocates a KV cache to use it as a scratch space and frequently update during verification stage.
proves: Memory model for Medusa trees: buffers scale with batch, tree nodes, candidates, levels, vocab; mask assumes full acceptance; pruning gives 65% runtime memory reduction keeping 96% throughput (Titan RTX 24 GB).
does_not_prove: Single-device, Medusa only; not a paged serving engine.
bearing: Threat to tree-buffer-shrinking ideas on small devices.

title: Speculative Speculative Decoding (Saguaro)
quote: necessitates a host-side post-processing step after each verification
proves: Saguaro's engine preempts sequences when lookahead reservations cannot be satisfied and deallocates pages beyond the accepted suffix after each verification; speculation cache is around hundreds of MB.
does_not_prove: No measurement of reservation-induced preemptions or host-side cost.
bearing: Shows reserve-then-reclaim with preemption is the standard pattern; cost of that pattern unmeasured.

title: Striking the Right Balance between Compute and Copy: Improving LLM Inferencing Under Speculative Decoding (BMC)
quote: This extra space can be repurposed for speculative decoding.
proves: BMC preallocates KV rows in chunks and uses the padding rows for speculative tokens (wasted rows 7 to 3 in an example); 1.23x geomean over vLLM. Notes vLLM allocates every 16 or 32 tokens.
does_not_prove: CPU-focused, OPT models; no high-load capacity measurement.
bearing: Partial threat: 'reuse padding for draft KV' is taken.

title: AdaServe: SLO-Customized LLM Serving with Fine-Grained Speculative Decoding
quote: The total number of nodes across all token trees must not exceed the hardware budget.
proves: Per-request minimum accepted tokens derived from TPOT SLO; per-step verification budget from hardware profiling split across requests' trees.
does_not_prove: Budget is compute per step; no KV memory accounting for trees.
bearing: Threat to SLO/latency-reservation-for-verification ideas: done for compute.

title: ECHO: Elastic Speculative Decoding with Sparse Gating for High-Concurrency Scenarios
quote: reformulates speculative execution as a budgeted scheduling problem
proves: High-concurrency regimes make verification compute dominant; static trees cause massive verification waste; ECHO in SGLang shifts budget between depth and width.
does_not_prove: Abstract only; compute budget, not memory reservation.
bearing: Threat to verify-budget ideas at high load.

title: TreeSpark: Calibrated, Load-Adaptive Draft Trees for Semi-Autoregressive Speculative Decoding
quote: gracefully shrinks the tree back to the chain
proves: Load-adaptive tree size: under rising load the tree shrinks to a chain; 15-25% more accepted tokens per round than a tuned chain.
does_not_prove: Does not discuss KV memory or reservation for tree nodes.
bearing: Threat: load-adaptive tree width (and hence its reservation) is covered for compute.

title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
quote: near-zero waste in KV cache memory
proves: Baseline: on-demand block allocation replaced max-length reservation, reducing KV waste from fragmentation and duplication and allowing larger batches.
does_not_prove: Predates spec-decode lookahead; does not cover per-step speculative reservation.
bearing: Known baseline: any reservation idea must beat on-demand + preemption.

title: Overcommit Accounting (Linux kernel docs)
quote: Heuristic overcommit handling. Obvious overcommits of address space are refused.
proves: OS baseline has three modes: heuristic (default), always overcommit, never overcommit (strict commit limit, allocations fail early instead of later kills).
does_not_prove: Analogy only. Maps to TRT-LLM (strict worst-case draft reserve, B15) vs vLLM (per-step optimistic lookahead with preemption, B1).
bearing: Frames a candidate: compare strict vs optimistic speculative reservation policies.

title: TransKV preprint on transactional speculative KV under paged memory (TechRxiv)
proves: Search snippet only: keeps speculative KV in a token-sized side buffer and commits accepted prefix to paged cache; up to 1.78x concurrency on P100/T4.
does_not_prove: Fetch failed (HTTP 403 via WebFetch and curl). Title, numbers and claims unverified.
bearing: If true, direct threat to a 'side buffer for speculative KV' idea; must be read before proposing one.

title: MineDraft: A Framework for Batch Parallel Speculative Decoding
quote: the performance of standard SD is often limited by the strictly sequential execution
proves: Two-batch overlap of drafting and verification as a vLLM plugin; up to 75% throughput gain.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not mention KV allocation; the search-snippet claim that it defers vLLM KV block allocation for drafted-but-unverified requests was not verified (PDF fetch exceeded size limit).
bearing: Possible threat to deferred-allocation ideas; verify full text.

title: Behind the Stack, Ep 13: Faster Inference: Speculative Decoding for Batched Workloads
quote: In high throughput workloads, the limiter is often KV cache capacity, not compute.
proves: Practitioner framing: when batch is KV-capacity bound, SD amortizes KV movement over more accepted tokens.
does_not_prove: Illustrative numbers only; does not quantify SD's own KV cost.
bearing: Supports that spec reservations matter exactly in the KV-bound regime where SD is pitched.

title: PipeSpec: Breaking Stage Dependencies in Hierarchical LLM Decoding
quote: enabling asynchronous execution with lightweight coordination for prediction verification and rollback
proves: Generalizes SD to k models in a pipeline across devices; claims guaranteed throughput improvement for any non-zero acceptance rate; up to 2.54x on LLaMA 2/3.
does_not_prove: Throughput guarantee is analytical and per-request, on dedicated devices; no shared-GPU or multi-request contention.
bearing: Prior art for multi-level pipelined speculation; threatens cascade-pipeline candidates.

title: SwiftSpec: Ultra-Low Latency LLM Decoding by Scaling Asynchronous Speculative Decoding
quote: redesigns the speculative decoding pipeline in an asynchronous and disaggregated manner
proves: Async disaggregated draft/verify removes draft from critical path; 1.75x avg over SOTA SD systems; Llama3-70B at 348 tok/s on 8 Hopper GPUs; targets single-query / small-batch TP.
does_not_prove: Small-batch latency only; no throughput-per-GPU or multi-tenant evaluation.
bearing: Threatens disaggregated async drafter ideas at batch 1; leaves high-batch and shared-drafter economics open.

title: NebulaSD: Many-for-Many Speculative Decoding
quote: dynamic pooling improves request-round processing rate by 50.4% over a physically disaggregated baseline
proves: M-for-N pooling of draft and target workers with batches rebuilt per stage from shared request pools and async KV-state preparation; +50.4% vs disaggregated, +72.6% vs co-located on 4 GPUs.
does_not_prove: Abstract only; scaling result is from idealized simulation of state movement; does not address mis-speculation waste or tenant isolation.
bearing: Strong threat to 'shared drafter pool / disaggregated drafting' candidates (very recent, Sep 2026).

title: ASPIRE: Asynchronous Batched Self-Speculative Decoding for Long-Context LLM Inference
quote: all requests in a batch share a single draft-verify schedule
proves: Non-synchronized batched self-speculation: batch-aware cost model lets each request choose when to verify; 1.70-4.58x decode throughput over AR; ~27% over best self-spec baselines.
does_not_prove: Self-speculative and long-context only; not a separate-drafter or engine (vLLM/SGLang) integration.
bearing: Threatens 'break lockstep draft/verify in a batch' candidates.

title: Cascade Speculative Drafting for Even Faster LLM Inference
quote: The Vertical Cascade eliminates autoregressive generation from neural models,
proves: Multi-level drafting: vertical cascade drafts the drafter; horizontal cascade allocates draft time by position.
does_not_prove: Abstract gives no numbers; sequential latency focus, no serving load.
bearing: Prior art for cascade/multi-level speculation.

title: LayerSkip: Enabling Early Exit Inference and Self-Speculative Decoding
quote: benefits from shared compute and activations of the draft and verification stages
proves: Early-exit drafting with remaining layers as verifier; less memory than separate drafter; up to 2.16x on CNN/DM.
does_not_prove: Requires training recipe; no batch/serving study.
bearing: Prior art for early-exit (confidence) drafting.

title: SpecReason: Fast and Accurate Inference-Time Compute via Speculative Reasoning
quote: SpecReason achieves 1.4-3.0
proves: Small model drafts whole reasoning steps; base model assesses/corrects them; 1.4-3.0x speedup with +0.4-9.0% accuracy; combined with SD an additional 8.8-58.0% latency reduction.
does_not_prove: Lossy (semantic not token equivalence); single-request; no serving cost of rejected steps under load.
bearing: Speculation beyond tokens; mis-speculation cost of rejected reasoning steps in shared serving is open.

title: HeteroReason: Heterogeneous FPGA-GPU Acceleration for Disaggregated Speculative Reasoning
quote: the draft model is offloaded to the FPGA while deploying the PRM and target models on GPUs.
proves: Disaggregated speculative reasoning with step-ahead speculation; 1.01x-1.42x latency, 1.25x-1.57x energy efficiency vs homogeneous GPU.
does_not_prove: FPGA-specific; small latency gains; no multi-tenant evaluation.
bearing: Supports 'drafter on separate cheap hardware' line; shows gains can be marginal.

title: Speculative Actions: A Lossless Framework for Faster Agentic Systems
quote: Across domains, we achieve up to 55% next-action prediction accuracy, translating into up to 20% latency reductions.
proves: Fast models predict next agent actions and execute in parallel, committed only when authoritative model agrees; gives a cost-latency analysis of speculative breadth.
does_not_prove: Cost figures not in abstract; does not study the serving engine side (extra requests' effect on other tenants' batches).
bearing: Threatens 'speculative tool calls' candidates; serving-side cost of agent speculation is open.

title: AOSpec: Action and Observation Co-Speculation for Low-Latency Agent Serving
quote: its gains increase as decoding accelerates
proves: Co-speculates actions and observations; side-effecting actions run in isolated forks; 11.8-32.5% mean and up to 42.8% p99 end-to-end latency reduction on Terminal-Bench.
does_not_prove: No detailed serving-cost figures in abstract; isolation is per-environment fork, not GPU/KV.
bearing: Strong threat to agent-level speculation candidates (Aug 2026).

title: Speculate with Memory: Lossless Acceleration for LLM Agents
quote: All speculation is lossless because it runs during idle time at zero added wall-clock cost.
proves: Memory of past trajectories improves action prediction 19-39% relative and observation prediction up to 2.5x.
does_not_prove: 'Zero added wall-clock cost' assumes idle resources; ignores GPU/token cost of speculative calls on a shared server.
bearing: The idle-time assumption is a gap: who pays for agent speculation on loaded servers.

title: Parallelizing Tool Execution and LLM Generation for Low-Latency Agent Serving (PASTE)
quote: PASTE isolates speculative results until confirmed by the LLM
proves: Speculative tool execution during generation; -43.5% avg task completion time; 1.8x lower observed tool latency.
does_not_prove: Abstract silent on mis-speculation cost / wasted tool calls.
bearing: Threatens speculative-tool-call candidates.

title: NVIDIA Dynamo docs: Agents user guide (speculative prefill)
quote: Per-turn TTFT on turns 2+ can drop significantly (e.g. up to ~3× in
proves: After a turn ends, Dynamo can send a speculative max_tokens=1 prefill of the predicted next-turn prefix to the same worker to warm KV; cache prefetching to other workers is listed as future work.
does_not_prove: No statement on wrong predictions, wasted prefill compute, or KV eviction pressure caused by speculative prefill under load.
bearing: Speculative prefill is shipped; its mis-speculation cost and KV-pressure interaction are open.

title: Async Scheduling Plan (vLLM issue #27679)
quote: Follow-on async scheduling + spec decode hardening/compatibility issues
proves: Tracking issue (Oct-Dec 2025) for async scheduling; lists #24799 spec compatibility, #29223 logprobs, #29821 structured outputs; closed via enabling async scheduling by default (#27614).
does_not_prove: Plan only; no performance data.
bearing: Shows async+spec is engine-level active work; context for engine candidates.

title: [Core] Async Scheduling X Spec Decoding Compatibility (vLLM PR #24799)
quote: we won't copy draft token ids to scheduler any more, but cache it in gpu_model_runner
proves: Drafts kept on GPU worker for next step; A100 EAGLE Llama3-8B k=2: +1.8% (24 prompts), +6.2% (48), +7.1% (96) throughput vs sync; only EAGLE supported at merge; blocking sync after drafting accepted as known compromise.
does_not_prove: Small gains; ngram/medusa excluded at merge; no mis-speculation accounting.
bearing: Baseline for vLLM async+spec; gains from overlap are modest.

title: [Async][Spec Decoding] Zero-bubble async scheduling + spec decoding (vLLM PR #32951)
quote: optimistically assuming all draft tokens are accepted on the CPU and deferring the correction until after the forward pass
proves: CPU schedules next step assuming all drafts accepted, GPU tensors are source of truth; DeepSeek-V3.2 MTP k=1 at concurrency 1: TPOT 9.19->8.90 ms, TTFT 62.86->53.30 ms.
does_not_prove: Benchmarked only at concurrency 1 with k=1 (94% acceptance); no data on how optimistic over-allocation behaves at low acceptance or high batch.
bearing: Optimistic placeholder scheduling = systems speculation inside engine; cost of over-reservation under load is open.

title: vLLM v0.19.0 release notes
quote: Async scheduling now supports speculative decoding with zero-bubble overlap, significantly improving throughput
proves: Zero-bubble async+spec shipped in v0.19.0 (#32951).
does_not_prove: Release note claim, no numbers.
bearing: Confirms feature is mainline; any candidate must start from it.

title: [Performance]: Eagle3 speculative decoding latency regression in v0.19 vs v0.18 (vLLM issue #39940)
quote: the regression cuts the spec decode benefit nearly in half
proves: H200 TP=4 Llama-3.1-8B + EAGLE3 k=3 at 1 QPS: TPOT 2.62 ms (v0.18) vs 2.84 ms (v0.19), spec speedup 16.0% -> 8.4%, acceptance unchanged; maintainer traced part to torch.compile of update_num_computed_tokens_for_batch_change (fix 2.82->2.63 ms) but said not sufficient; closed as stale.
does_not_prove: Single low-load workload; root cause not fully closed.
bearing: Evidence that async+spec bookkeeping (small kernels) eats spec gains; supports measurement-driven candidates.

title: [Bug]: PP + async scheduling + spec decode: output_token_ids trim only runs on the last PP rank (vLLM issue #54260)
quote: With pipeline parallelism, async scheduling and speculative decoding active at the same time, the non-last ranks accumulate an unbounded overshoot
proves: Optimistic extend (assumes all k drafts accepted) never trimmed on non-last PP ranks; NCCL deadlock after ~15 rounds; reproduced on v0.27.1 with PP=2 + MTP k=7; open as of Aug 2026.
does_not_prove: Correctness bug, not a performance study.
bearing: Shows rollback of optimistic state is fragile across ranks; supports 'rollback correctness/cost' angle.

title: [Bug]: json_object structured output not enforced after Qwen thinking with async scheduling + spec decode (vLLM issue #43388)
quote: in async scheduling + speculative decoding, new_token_ids can contain multiple tokens in one step
proves: Multi-token accepted steps plus placeholder offsets made the reasoning-end detector miss </think>, so the grammar was never applied.
does_not_prove: Correctness bug; closed.
bearing: Interaction bugs between optimistic placeholders and per-token state machines.

title: SGLang docs: Speculative Decoding (V2 / overlap scheduler)
quote: The overlap scheduler currently only supports `--speculative-eagle-topk 1`
proves: Spec V2 workers run with overlap scheduler by default; NGRAM and DFLASH disable the overlap scheduler and mixed chunked prefill; topk>1 errors or is incompatible.
does_not_prove: Docs; no performance numbers.
bearing: Shows overlap is limited to chain drafts; tree/ngram overlap is a remaining engine gap.

title: From research to production: Accelerate OSS LLM with EAGLE-3 on Vertex
quote: the overlap scheduler gives us an additional 10% - 20% speedup across the board
proves: CPU launches next Draft and Draft Extend kernels while GPU runs Verify, via a FutureMap; +10-20% on Llama 4 Scout.
does_not_prove: Configuration for the number not given; vendor blog.
bearing: Overlap of CPU scheduling with verify is largely captured already.

title: [Spec] DFlash: remove per-step host syncs so the CPU runs a full step ahead (SGLang PR #31468)
quote: worth **+12–13% tok/s/user at low concurrency and +3–5% at high**
proves: Removing per-step host syncs raised run-ahead fraction 0.88 -> 0.995; gain +12-13% at low concurrency, +3-5% at high; GSM8K and accept length unchanged.
does_not_prove: Single proposer (DFlash); H-class GPU only.
bearing: Quantifies that overlap gains shrink at high concurrency.

title: [SPEC V2] fix: skip stale state updates in spec-v2 overlap (SGLang PR #23456)
quote: only rolls back the pre-claimed bonus slot for finished requests
proves: Under overlap, decode results can arrive after a request finished or was retracted; applying accept_lens to stale requests corrupted KV bookkeeping and spec metrics.
does_not_prove: Bug fix, no measurement.
bearing: Speculative pre-claim of KV slots before acceptance is real engine practice; rollback paths are bug-prone.

title: Fix cross-stream ordering races in spec-v2 overlap plan stream (SGLang PR #28034)
quote: silently degrading accuracy and accept length
proves: With the overlap plan stream on, prepare_for_v2_verify overwrote shared req_to_token cells while draft still read them; under load crashed with illegal memory access; open PR.
does_not_prove: Opt-in flag only; no perf numbers.
bearing: Further evidence that deeper overlap of draft/verify planning hits shared-state hazards.

title: Support spec v2 tree drafting (eagle topk>1) with page_size==1 (SGLang PR #26866)
quote: topk>1 with page_size>1 still falls back to v1.
proves: Tree drafting under overlap scheduler now works only for page_size==1; accepted-KV move had been stubbed.
does_not_prove: No throughput numbers.
bearing: Tree speculation + overlap + paged KV remains incomplete in SGLang.

title: Nightjar: Dynamic Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Large Language Models Serving
quote: while retaining the draft model reduces KV cache capacity, limiting batch size and degrading throughput
proves: SD degrades performance in high-load compute-bound settings; Nightjar disables SD under load and offloads drafter; up to 14.76% throughput and 20.18% lower latency vs standard SD.
does_not_prove: Adaptive on/off is R04 territory; does not study overlapped/async speculation costs.
bearing: Evidence that speculation hurts at high batch; threatens naive always-on overlap ideas.

title: An Interpretable Latency Model for Speculative Decoding in LLM Serving
quote: explains why speedups often diminish as server load increases
proves: Latency model infers effective batch size from request rate via Little's Law to explain shrinking SD gains under load.
does_not_prove: Abstract gives no thresholds; does not model async/overlapped drafting.
bearing: Supports a model-based answer to 'when does speculation hurt'; async variants not modelled.

title: Batch speculative decoding (EQSPEC) ragged-tensor overhead
proves: Search snippet only: fixing ragged acceptance across a batch adds overhead up to 40% of compute.
does_not_prove: Not opened; venue and numbers unverified.
bearing: Possible cost of per-request acceptance divergence at batch.

title: vLLM v0.18.0 release notes (NGram GPU + async scheduler, #29184)
proves: Search snippet only: NGram speculative decoding runs on GPU and is compatible with the async scheduler.
does_not_prove: Not opened.
bearing: If true, ngram async gap in vLLM is closed (unlike SGLang C26).

title: Taming the Long-Tail: Efficient Reasoning RL Training with Adaptive Drafter
quote: activates SD only when the remaining request count drops below a configurable threshold (default: 32)
proves: Drafter is trained continuously on GPUs idled by the RL rollout long tail; a Worker Coordinator moves idle workers busy->idle->training, drafter updates are preemptible low-priority spot tasks with async checkpoints, halted when rollout ends; rollout ~85% of step time; >1.7x end-to-end RL speedup; SD only below 32 remaining requests; switching to SD costs a ~3 s re-prefill.
does_not_prove: Idle harvesting only exists because synchronous RL has a known end-of-step barrier; nothing about serving with open-ended arrivals; no idle-GPU fraction given; drafter trained every ~10 steps suffices, so the idle budget needed is small and unquantified.
bearing: Directly occupies 'train drafter on idle GPUs' and 'spec only for stragglers' in RL; threatens any RL-rollout idle-harvest candidate.

title: Beat the long tail: Distribution-Aware Speculative Decoding for RL Training
venue: arXiv 2511.13841 (MLSys 2026 per proceedings link in search)
quote: a length aware speculation policy that allocates more aggressive draft budgets to long trajectories that dominate makespan
proves: Training-free suffix-tree drafter built from recent rollouts across epochs, plus length-aware draft budgets for long trajectories; up to 50% rollout-time reduction with identical training curves.
does_not_prove: Draft source is cross-epoch history of same prompts, not cross-request in a serving batch; budget allocation is per-trajectory within one engine, not across replicas.
bearing: Occupies 'cross-request/history suffix drafting for RL stragglers' and 'give stragglers more speculation budget'.

title: BubbleSpec: Turning Long-Tail Bubbles into Speculative Rollout Drafts for Synchronous Reinforcement Learning
venue: arXiv 2605.08862 (ICML 2026 poster per icml.cc listing in search)
quote: These bubbles can account for more than 60% of the total rollout time.
proves: Faster DP ranks use idle bubble time to pre-generate next-step rollouts, stored as a suffix tree draft database; bubbles average >1/3 of rollout time, max >2/3; acceptance only ~22-30%, mean accepted ~2 tokens; 50% fewer decoding steps, up to 1.8x rollout throughput; using intra-GPU bubbles slowed the current batch so only inter-GPU bubbles used.
does_not_prove: Single node 8 GPUs only; sync RL only, async not evaluated; no test with zero bubble; rollout time falls less than step count because verification runs at larger batch.
bearing: Strongest prior art for 'idle ranks do speculative work for others'; also evidence that same-GPU harvesting hurts the main batch.

title: TailSieve: Partial-Rollout-Guided Tail Routing for LLM Rollouts
quote: a small number of long-tail generations can dominate the end-to-end makespan of an entire rollout step
proves: Routes likely-tail prompts (detected from partial rollouts) to a low-concurrency tail pool; top-k policy approximates offline optimum; up to 1.67x from routing alone and 2.59x with route-specialized MTP or DFlash speculation on the tail pool.
does_not_prove: RL rollout only; replica pools are re-sized by a controller, not per-request work stealing in serving; does not study moving in-flight requests once speculation speeds diverge.
bearing: Occupies 'route stragglers to low-batch replicas where speculation is cheap'; closest to cross-replica load balancing with spec.

title: Online Speculative Decoding
quote: the surplus computational power in a typical LLM serving cluster can be repurposed for online retraining of draft models
proves: Original claim that spare serving FLOPs (non-spike windows) can retrain drafters online via distillation; gradient updates only when traffic not on spike; acceptance +0.1 to 0.65, latency 1.42x-2.17x.
does_not_prove: Does not measure how much spare compute exists or the interference of training with serving; prototype-level, not a production scheduler.
bearing: Foundational prior art for 'train drafter on idle serving capacity'.

title: When RL Meets Adaptive Speculative Training: A Unified Training-Serving System (Aurora)
quote: hot-swapped speculator updates without service interruption
proves: Async training server learns a speculator from live inference traces and hot-swaps it into SGLang; 1.5x day-0 speedup on new frontier models, extra 1.25x over static speculator under traffic shift.
does_not_prove: Abstract gives no GPU cost of the training server or whether it uses idle serving capacity; separate trainer rather than harvested cycles.
bearing: Occupies 'continuous drafter adaptation in production'; leaves open who pays for training compute.

title: SpecPipe: Accelerating Pipeline Parallelism-based LLM Inference with Speculative Decoding
quote: fills the pipeline with speculative tokens of a request step-by-step
proves: Fills pipeline-parallel stages with speculative tokens from a token tree; 8-stage pipeline: 4.19x-5.53x better TBT than plain PP for single request; SpecPipe-DB 1.64x-2.08x throughput vs vLLM for multi-request.
does_not_prove: Results for one 8-stage setup; single-request focus; ideal one-token-per-step is not measured.
bearing: Occupies 'fill PP bubbles with speculation'.

title: Speculative Pipeline Decoding: Higher-Accuracy Drafting with Hidden Latency via Pipeline Parallelism
quote: partitions the target LLM into $n$ pipeline stages
proves: Splits target into pipeline stages to hide draft latency, beating EAGLE-3 at moderate pipeline width; targets low-concurrency SD.
does_not_prove: No numbers in abstract; larger widths still leave room; low-concurrency only.
bearing: Further occupies PP-bubble speculation; space for high-batch PP still open.

title: Fast LLM Post-training via Decoupled and Fastest-of-N Speculation (SpecActor)
quote: with relative large per-worker batch size
proves: Decoupled speculation fixes SD compute inefficiency at large per-worker batch (common in training, unfriendly to speculation); Fastest-of-N picks draft method by rollout progress; 2.0-2.4x mean rollout speedup, 1.4-2.3x end-to-end.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not mention using idle GPUs; RL-only.
bearing: Evidence that large batch kills free speculation; occupies 'decouple draft from verify to run on other resources' in RL.

title: Seer: Online Context Learning for Fast Synchronous LLM Reinforcement Learning
quote: adaptive grouped speculative decoding to accelerate generation
proves: Divided rollout for dynamic load balancing plus grouped speculative decoding using same-prompt group similarity; up to 2.04x rollout throughput, long-tail latency down 72-94%.
does_not_prove: Group siblings as draft source is specific to GRPO-style multi-sample prompts; not serving.
bearing: Occupies 'steal draft tokens from sibling requests' and load balancing with spec in RL.

title: FastGRPO: Accelerating Policy Optimization via Concurrency-aware Speculative Decoding and Online Draft Learning
quote: its direct application in GRPO achieves limited speedup under high-concurrency training conditions
proves: SD gives limited speedup at high concurrency; concurrency-aware drafting/verify strategy plus online draft learning from target feedback; 2.35x-2.72x end-to-end.
does_not_prove: Online draft learning cost and placement not in abstract.
bearing: Negative result on SD at high concurrency; occupies online drafter adaptation in RL.

title: History Rhymes: Accelerating LLM Reinforcement Learning with RhymeRL
venue: arXiv 2508.18588 (ASPLOS 26 per SJTU pdf name in search)
quote: Imbalances in rollout lengths (within the same batch) result in GPU bubbles
proves: HistoSpec uses previous-epoch rollouts as drafts; HistoPipe balances workload by historical length distributions; 2.6x; production scale dozens to thousands of GPUs.
does_not_prove: Relies on cross-epoch similarity; no first-epoch benefit (noted by BubbleSpec).
bearing: Occupies history-based drafting plus balancing for RL.

title: APRIL: Active Partial Rollouts in Reinforcement Learning to Tame Long-tail Generation
quote: a few lengthy responses stall entire batches, leaving GPUs idle and underutilized
proves: Rollout >90% of runtime; over-provision rollouts, stop at target count, carry unfinished ones forward; +22.5% avg (max 44%) throughput.
does_not_prove: No speculative decoding; it removes the idle bubble that spec-harvesting systems rely on.
bearing: Competing non-spec fix that can make the idle window vanish.

title: MagicDec: Breaking the Latency-Throughput Tradeoff for Long Context Generation with Speculative Decoding
quote: MagicDec first identifies the bottleneck shifts with increasing batch size and sequence length
proves: With long context, KV loading (scales with batch and length) stays the bottleneck so SD helps at batch 32-256: up to 2.51x for Llama3.1-8B.
does_not_prove: Only long-context regime; short-context high-batch decode is still compute-limited for verification.
bearing: Defines when idle compute exists at large batch; supports spec at large batch only for long context.

title: TurboSpec: Closed-loop Speculation Control System for Optimizing LLM Serving Goodput
quote: speculative decoding may degrade LLM serving performance if added naively
proves: Speculation adds overhead and misses; runtime feedback control of speculation depth for goodput in vLLM.
does_not_prove: Does not quantify idle compute; per-engine control, not cross-replica.
bearing: Negative evidence: speculation is not free under load.

title: AgentSpec: Speculative Decoding for Batch Inference of LLM Agents
quote: state-of-the-art speculative decoding algorithms exhibit substantial speed degradation under large batch sizes
proves: SD degrades at large batch from high rejection and under-used dynamic token budgets; proposes structure-isolated drafting and redundancy-aware budget allocation in vLLM.
does_not_prove: Abstract gives no batch-size numbers.
bearing: Recent negative evidence on large-batch SD; occupies batch-level token-budget allocation.

title: SPIRe: Boosting LLM Inference Throughput with Speculative Decoding
quote: Recent work shows that SD can accelerate decoding with large batch sizes too if the context is sufficiently long
proves: Draft design for throughput; >100% modeled throughput gain over small draft, >35% over sparse self-speculation; gains largest when context lengths vary across requests.
does_not_prove: Throughput is modeled, not measured end to end.
bearing: Supports that high-batch spec depends on context; modeled only.

title: EAGLE-3: Scaling up Inference Acceleration of Large Language Models via Training-Time Test
quote: In the SGLang framework, EAGLE-3 achieves a 1.38x throughput improvement at a batch size of 64.
proves: EAGLE-3 still gives 1.38x throughput at batch 64 in SGLang.
does_not_prove: Single data point; does not show where gain hits zero.
bearing: Bounds how quickly idle compute disappears for strong drafters.

title: TensorRT-LLM Speculative Decoding docs (n-gram is_public_pool)
quote: If true, a single ngram pool is shared for all requests. Otherwise, each request has its own ngram pool.
proves: Production engine already supports one n-gram draft pool shared across all requests.
does_not_prove: No measurements of cross-request acceptance gain or isolation/privacy implications; suffix automaton scope not stated.
bearing: Occupies basic 'steal draft tokens across requests'; leaves tenant isolation of shared pool open.

title: SuffixDecoding: Extreme Speculative Decoding for Emerging AI Applications
quote: utilizes efficient suffix trees to cache long token sequences from prompts and previous outputs
proves: Model-free suffix-tree drafting from prompts and prior outputs; up to 5.3x on SWE-Bench and Text-to-SQL; 2.8x over EAGLE-2/3.
does_not_prove: Abstract alone does not show cross-tenant sharing policy or CPU cost.
bearing: Occupies cross-request history drafting in serving.

title: SuffixDecoding at Production Scale with Arctic Inference and vLLM
quote: Since SuffixDecoding runs on CPU, its latency scales linearly with the number of speculated tokens
proves: One global suffix tree caches responses from previous requests; drafting runs on CPU, ~20-30 us per speculated token early on; remaining overhead ~10% at concurrency 64 after optimization; eviction supported.
does_not_prove: No multi-tenant/privacy treatment; no measurement of whether CPU drafting steals host cycles needed by the scheduler.
bearing: Shows CPU drafting is on the critical path at high concurrency; cross-tenant sharing isolation unaddressed.

title: How Speculative Decoding Boosts vLLM Performance by up to 2.8x
quote: As high QPS, we see 1.4x slowdown Llama3-70B on ShareGPT with 4xH100
proves: At high QPS speculation slowed Llama3-70B by 1.4x on 4xH100 because propose/verify compute hurts when already compute-bound; up to 1.5x (draft) and 2.8x (prompt lookup) at low QPS.
does_not_prove: Old vLLM V0 implementation; no batch-size crossover curve.
bearing: Negative evidence: 'free' compute vanishes at high load.

title: ATLAS: AdapTive-LeArning Speculator System
quote: The acceptance rate rises from below 10% to above 80% over 1.4k training steps
proves: Production adaptive speculator learning from live traffic plus static speculator and controller; up to 500 TPS DeepSeek-V3.1 at batch 1 on B200; in RL acceptance <10% to >80%, >60% training time cut; RL rollouts ~70% of wall-clock.
does_not_prove: Does not say what compute the adaptive training runs on; headline numbers at batch 1.
bearing: Occupies production online drafter adaptation; compute accounting open.

title: Nightjar: Dynamic Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Large Language Models Serving
quote: retaining the draft model reduces KV cache capacity, limiting batch size and degrading throughput
proves: MAB planner disables SD when not beneficial and offloads draft model to reclaim KV memory; up to 14.76% more throughput than standard SD, 20.18% lower latency.
does_not_prove: Single-engine policy; no cross-replica or idle-harvest dimension.
bearing: Negative evidence: drafter memory competes with batch; spec stops being free in memory too.

title: Harli: SLO-Aware Co-location of LLM Inference and PEFT-based Finetuning on Model-as-a-Service Platforms
quote: the average SM utilization remains as low as 40%
proves: On LLaMA3-8B decode (Ada6000), DRAM bandwidth ~85% but SM ~40%; co-locates PEFT finetuning with decode for +46.2% avg finetune throughput under decode QoS.
does_not_prove: Harvests idle SMs for finetuning, not for speculation or drafter training; single GPU type.
bearing: Quantifies idle compute in decode; a competing consumer of the same idle SMs (drafter training could be the PEFT job).

title: SpecEdge: Scalable Edge-Assisted Serving Framework for Interactive LLMs
quote: proactive edge drafting to overlap edge token creation with server verification
proves: Drafting on consumer edge GPUs overlapping server verification; 1.91x cost efficiency, 2.22x server throughput, 11.24% lower ITL.
does_not_prove: Edge-cloud network setting; not idle datacenter resources.
bearing: Occupies 'draft on someone else's idle device'.

title: Online Draft Co-Training for Speculative Decoding in Large-Scale, Long-Context RL Post-Training
quote: TapChannel transports intermediate target features across stages via a separate path, leaving the pipeline schedule unaffected
proves: Co-trains the draft alongside policy training with PP feature transport and CP at 256K; scales to 122B.
does_not_prove: Abstract gives no speedup numbers or whether co-training uses idle resources.
bearing: Latest (Sep 2026) entrant in online drafter training for RL.

title: Accelerating RL Post-Training Rollouts via System-Integrated Speculative Decoding
quote: improves rollout throughput by 1.8x
proves: NeMo-RL + vLLM SD for sync and async RL; 1.8x rollout throughput at 8B sync; projected (simulated) 2.5x end-to-end at 235B with async.
does_not_prove: Async gain is simulated, not measured; abstract silent on batch-size limits.
bearing: Shows SD is now standard in RL stacks; async+SD interplay lightly measured.

title: Speculative Decoding: Performance or Illusion?
venue: arXiv 2601.11580 v1 (MLSys 2026 per mlsys.org in search)
quote: Increasing batch size improves absolute throughput but systematically reduces the relative speedup
proves: Systematic vLLM study on H100: verification dominates execution; EAGLE speedup on Llama3.1-8B GSM8K falls from 1.73x at batch 1 to 1.21x at batch 128; large gaps to theoretical bounds.
does_not_prove: Up to batch 128 mostly; does not locate the zero-gain crossover; vLLM 0.10.1.1.
bearing: Key evidence on how fast idle compute shrinks; real gains persist to batch 128 for 8B.

title: PipeInfer: Accelerating LLM Inference using Asynchronous Pipelined Speculation
venue: arXiv 2407.11798 (SC 2024 per TU Darmstadt bibtex in search)
quote: pipeline-parallel designs require many user requests to maintain maximum utilization
proves: Continuous asynchronous speculation and early cancellation fill PP stages for single requests; up to 2.15x over standard speculative inference.
does_not_prove: Single-request, llama.cpp/MPI cluster; not multi-tenant batch.
bearing: Occupies PP-bubble speculation for single request.

title: Laminar: A Scalable Asynchronous RL Post-Training Framework
quote: a dynamic repack mechanism consolidates long-tail trajectories onto a few dedicated rollouts
proves: Repacks long-tail trajectories onto few rollouts to free others; up to 5.48x training throughput on 1024 GPUs.
does_not_prove: No speculative decoding; repacking raises batch on destination, which would shrink spec benefit there.
bearing: Competing non-spec fix; also shows request migration across rollout replicas already exists.

title: RollPacker: Mitigating Long-Tail Rollouts for Fast, Synchronous RL Post-Training
quote: systematically consolidates prompts leading to long-tail responses into a small subset of rollout steps
proves: Tail batching; 2.03x-2.56x end-to-end vs veRL, up to 2.24x vs RLHFuse on up to 128 H800.
does_not_prove: No speculative decoding in abstract.
bearing: Competing scheduling fix that removes idle windows.

title: Accelerate RL rollouts by up to 50% with distribution-aware speculative decoding
quote: DAS therefore uses a training-free drafter built from recent rollouts, so it can continuously adapt to the changing policy
proves: Suffix-tree construction/cleanup parallelized per problem and overlapped with actor updates; >50% rollout reduction math RL, ~25-30% code RL.
does_not_prove: Does not say CPU vs GPU for drafting.
bearing: Shows draft-structure building already hidden in idle training phase.

title: SuffixGPU (PyPI suffix-gpu)
proves: Search snippet claimed cross-request global memory on a GPU suffix array.
does_not_prove: Fetch failed (page did not render); unverified.
bearing: Possible prior art for GPU-side cross-request drafting.

title: ConServe (co-serving online and offline work to harvest idle GPU cycles)
proves: Search snippet: layer-wise preemption to co-serve offline work in idle GPU cycles.
does_not_prove: Not opened.
bearing: Mechanism a drafter-training-on-idle-serving design would need.

title: Tackling the Data-Parallel Load Balancing Bottleneck in LLM Serving (BalanceRoute)
proves: Search snippet: DP routing is sticky since KV caches cannot be migrated.
does_not_prove: Not opened; no spec decode link known.
bearing: Relevant to cross-replica rebalancing when spec speeds diverge.

title: [Spec] Enable adaptive speculative decoding under DP attention (PR #35898)
quote: under skewed load `min` pins every rank to the lowest tier a neighbor wants, so a light rank can lose speculation it could afford
proves: SGLang disables adaptive draft depth under DP attention because ranks choosing different num_steps change the shape of the cross-rank MLP-sync all_gather and NCCL hangs. The PR agrees a tier by min() over ranks on the existing all_gather; 4xH200 tp4/dp2/ep4 EAGLE GSM8K: adaptive = fixed (116 tok/s at c1, 548 at c8, accept_len ~3.25). PR closed unmerged.
does_not_prove: No result on a low-acceptance or skewed workload; the cost of min-consensus (light ranks losing speculation) is stated, not measured. No per-rank speculation (different K per rank with shape padding) was tried.
bearing: Supports: per-DP-rank speculation depth under a lockstep collective is an open, acknowledged problem

title: [Spec] Stabilize the DP adaptive tier vote: shared EMA + min dwell (PR #39231)
quote: `min()` over 8 noisy per-rank EMAs sits below the mean at dp-rank BS~1, so alternating is the *steady state*, not an accident.
proves: GLM-5.2 tp8/dp8/ep8: min-of-8 DP tier vote thrashed ~1100 tier switches/h at c8 (298/h c16, 56/h c24), c16 ITL p95 +14% vs fixed. Fix (shared mean EMA over the all_gather + min dwell 50 batches) cut to 1 switch over the whole ladder; throughput -1.2% to +2.9% vs fixed EAGLE. Closed unmerged.
does_not_prove: Fix replaces min with a fleet mean, so every rank runs one tier; it does not let ranks with different acceptance run different depths. Single runs; no skewed-acceptance workload.
bearing: Supports: DP-wide speculation control is fragile; per-rank heterogeneity is averaged away, not exploited

title: Dynamic speculative decoding (vLLM docs)
quote: Each DP rank schedules independently, so ranks can pick different K values, causing DP collective divergence and deadlocks.
proves: vLLM maps concurrency ranges to K (example: K=3 at 1-64, K=1 at 65-128, K=0 at 129-512) and automatically disables num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size when DP is enabled, falling back to static K.
does_not_prove: Does not quantify what static K costs under DP; no cross-rank agreement mechanism exists in vLLM per this page.
bearing: Supports: load-adaptive speculation is turned OFF exactly in DP+EP MoE deployments; a gap in vLLM

title: [Bug]: vLLM hangs during speculative decoding with MoE draft model near max_model_len under Data Parallelism (DP) (issue #44185)
quote: When running vLLM with Speculative Decoding enabled, the server permanently hangs (deadlocks) under the following specific conditions:
proves: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, DP=2 + EP + MTP K=3: a request near max_model_len makes one DP rank skip drafting while the other enters the MoE drafter forward, so the collective never completes. Opened 2026-06-01, still open.
does_not_prove: A correctness bug, not a performance study; says nothing about the throughput cost of forcing all ranks to draft.
bearing: Supports: per-rank speculation decisions must be globally agreed under DP+EP; local choice deadlocks

title: Fix DP drafter hang near max model length (PR #44954)
quote: This PR fixes a vLLM hang during MTP speculative decoding with DP + EP near `max_model_len`.
proves: Fix for E4; notes the same issue was already fixed in vllm-ascend. Open (unmerged) as of today.
does_not_prove: No performance data; no general per-rank speculation-agreement design.
bearing: Same as E4: engines handle DP speculation by forcing uniformity

title: [Scheduler] Skip the spec + DP prefill-first MLP sync while no rank has prefill work (PR #42462)
quote: so a decode step pays two barriers instead of one
proves: With spec decode + DP attention, SGLang runs an extra prefill-first CPU all_gather each step so prefill and verify batches never mix across ranks. 8xB200 DeepSeek-V4-Flash DSpark ~50 req/rank: 2 gloo all_gathers/step, 9.4 ms waiting per 48.9 ms step (GPU kernels 21.9 ms). Skipping it when no rank has prefill: ~7% faster batch run (131 s -> 119-125 s). Open.
