does_not_prove: Gain only when no rank has queued prefill (offline batch); continuous arrivals keep the barrier. Profiler inflates host time. Does not separate skew from acceptance vs skew from batch size.
bearing: Supports: speculation forces DP phase lockstep; the rank-skew barrier is a large share of step time

title: [Fix] spec: Remove `--speculative-skip-dp-mlp-sync` (PR #45043)
quote: the flag let one DP rank prefill while another decoded, which sent the decoding rank's batch into the prefill path, raised `AttributeError` and took the server down
proves: Merged 2026-10-18. The option that let spec-decode DP ranks run different phases was removed; the pre-sync now always runs unless SGLANG_ENABLE_DP_SPEC_PREFILL_COORDINATION is on.
does_not_prove: No performance numbers; does not describe how the coordination env var works.
bearing: Supports: decoupling DP ranks under speculation is still unsolved in SGLang as of last week

title: scheduler: opt-in DP-attention phase lockstep (--enable-dp-phase-lockstep) (PR #37273)
quote: generalizes the spec-decode path's prefill-first sync to non-spec serving
proves: Under DP attention any mixed decode+extend pass runs eager on every rank. Forcing phase lockstep (as spec decode already does) raised throughput 21-45% at c50-c200 on tp4/dp4 MoE with long prompts, TPOT p90 58->33 ms at c50.
does_not_prove: Non-spec workload; does not measure what lockstep costs spec decode when ranks have unequal acceptance or batch sizes.
bearing: Threatens a naive 'remove lockstep' idea: lockstep can be the faster design

title: Add DP-Draft to run draft model with TP=1 (PR #17418)
quote: For MoE drafts, EP=1 concentrates all experts on a single GPU and can lead to more fragmented kernel shapes, so throughput may not improve.
proves: Running the draft per-GPU at TP=1 while the target runs TP16/EP16 DP attention: Kimi-K2 4k/1.5k decode per GPU 1.87x at bs1 falling to 1.20x at bs32; on GSM8K Kimi-K2 DP-Draft 3173 tok/s vs 3466 no-draft (slower), DeepSeek-R1 NEXTN 3441 vs 3195 (faster). Closed unmerged.
does_not_prove: Speedup shrinks with batch; no tail or per-rank imbalance data; not adopted upstream.
bearing: Supports: drafter placement across DP ranks is a live design axis; speedup collapses at batch 32

title: [DSpark] Enable compact DP tier synchronization for PD decode (PR #37763)
quote: DSpark compact verification with DP Attention requires all participating DP ranks to select the same CUDA Graph verify tier.
proves: Verify CUDA-graph tier must be identical across DP ranks; on PD decode servers it was pinned (graph_tier=pinned), losing compact-verify benefit. PR gathers tier across ranks. Open.
does_not_prove: Speed numbers truncated in what I read; tier is a max over ranks, so per-rank verify width still cannot differ.
bearing: Supports: verify width is forced uniform across DP ranks; per-rank verify sizing is open

title: [Bug] EAGLE + DP attention: idle verify crashes (issue #43287)
quote: a DP rank that has no requests in a step crashes in the target verify
proves: Under EAGLE + DP attention an idle DP rank must still run a padded idle verify forward each step so collectives line up; a single in-flight request is enough to trigger the idle path.
does_not_prove: Bug report; no measurement of how much compute idle-rank verify padding wastes.
bearing: Supports: idle/light DP ranks pay full verify-shaped work; wasted-work accounting is open

title: [3/N] [spec] support STANDALONE spec decoding with DP attention (PR #30877)
quote: STANDALONE spec decoding and DP attention are mutually exclusive.
proves: As of 2026-07 separate-draft-model spec decode could not run with DP attention in SGLang; PR enables topk=1, attn_tp=1 only; Qwen3-30B-A3B + Qwen3-0.6B tp4/dp4 accept length 4.00 vs 3.95 without DP. Open.
does_not_prove: Correctness-only; no throughput or imbalance data; MoE drafts and PD untested.
bearing: Supports: DP + draft-model combos are immature; many configurations not even runnable

title: Eagle3 DP attention for Qwen3 MoE (PR #12002)
quote: Add eagle3 dp attention for Qwen3 MoE model for large scale EP deployment.
proves: Merged 2025-10-29. Shows a production-style decode config: EAGLE3 (3 steps, topk 3, 8 draft tokens) + DP attention + DeepEP low_latency + EPLB + --load-balance-method round_robin; 8xH100 GSM8K 565 tok/s.
does_not_prove: DP request placement is round_robin, blind to acceptance; no imbalance measurement.
bearing: Supports: DP dispatch in spec-decode deployments ignores acceptance

title: [v1] align execute_dummy_batch with uniform decode query length (PR #37142)
quote: When spec decode is enabled, `uniform_decode_query_len` becomes `1 + num_speculative_tokens`.
proves: In vLLM DP, idle ranks run dummy batches; with spec decode the dummy must be padded to 1+K tokens per request to match peers (DeepSeek-V3.2 + MTP + DP on B300). Closed unmerged.
does_not_prove: No cost measurement of padding idle ranks to verify shape.
bearing: Supports: idle-rank verify padding is real wasted work under DP

title: Accelerating SGLang with Multiple Token Prediction
quote: Data-Parallel Attention (DP Attention)
proves: MTP is integrated with DP attention, EPLB, DeepEP, TBO. Gains: +59.8% (3-token) / +60.8% (4-token) at 2 concurrent req per rank, accept length 2.18/2.44; only +14.2% at 128 concurrent req per rank. Advises draft size 2-3 under large batches.
does_not_prove: The two cases differ in hardware and settings; no per-DP-rank acceptance or imbalance data.
bearing: Supports: speculation gain shrinks with per-rank batch; DP-rank interaction unmeasured

title: DeepSeek-V3/R1 Inference System Overview (Day 6, open-infra-index)
quote: Uneven request counts and sequence lengths across DP instances cause disparities in core-attention computation
proves: DeepSeek runs three load balancers: prefill, decode (balance KV usage and request counts per GPU) and expert-parallel (minimize max dispatch receive load). Decode averages 20-22 tok/s per request, ~14.8k output tok/s per H800 node.
does_not_prove: The page does not mention MTP or acceptance; the decode LB balances request counts and KV, not tokens-per-step or acceptance.
bearing: Supports: production DP decode balancers are acceptance-blind

title: Pushing the Limits of Serving DeepSeek-V4-Pro
quote: DSpark traffic also exhibits significant expert skew.
proves: On H20 DP32-EP32 decode, they recorded routing from representative DSpark (speculative) requests and used it to configure EPLB and redundant experts: +13.5% per-GPU throughput. Also 319.92 -> 703.15 tok/s/GPU at 4K, 32 req per DP rank.
does_not_prove: Does not show that the skew is caused by verify tokens (vs plain decode); offline-profiled placement, not online.
bearing: Partly threatens 'verify-aware EPLB' as novel; supports: speculation-shaped expert skew is real and costly

title: Scaling Large MoE Models with Wide Expert Parallelism on NVL72 Rack Scale Systems
quote: In testing, large EP configurations reached up to 1.8x higher per-GPU throughput than smaller EP setups.
proves: TRT-LLM Wide-EP with online EPLB; EP32 vs EP8 comparison used disaggregated serving and MTP in both arms.
does_not_prove: MTP is held constant; no analysis of how MTP verify tokens change expert load or EPLB.
bearing: Neutral: confirms MTP + wide EP is standard, interaction unstudied

title: Utility-Driven Speculative Decoding for Mixture-of-Experts (Cascade)
quote: draft tokens collectively activate more weights, increasing data movement and verification time by 2-3x.
proves: In MoE, speculation can slow decode up to 1.5x; Cascade turns speculation on/off and tunes K by utility, limiting slowdown to 5% and +7-14% throughput vs static K.
does_not_prove: Single-node data movement view; nothing on EP all-to-all, per-rank receive load or DP.
bearing: Threatens 'MoE spec on/off by utility' as novel; leaves EP/DP version open

title: MoE-Spec: Expert Budgeting for Efficient Speculative Decoding
quote: large draft trees activate many unique experts, significantly increasing memory pressure
proves: Capping experts loaded per layer during verification gives 10-30% higher throughput than EAGLE-3.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not mention expert parallelism or batch size.
bearing: Threatens expert-budget verification ideas; EP-rank balance open

title: Less Experts, Faster Decoding: Cost-Aware Speculative Decoding for Mixture-of-Experts (EcoSpec)
quote: may route to disjoint experts, increasing expert-weight memory traffic
proves: Adds predicted marginal expert-activation cost to draft selection; up to 1.62x speedup.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not cover batched decoding or multi-GPU expert placement.
bearing: Threatens expert-aware draft selection; EP-rank load version open

title: Making Every Verified Token Count: Adaptive Verification for MoE Speculative Decoding (EVICT)
quote: expanding the union of activated experts and substantially increasing target-side verification cost
proves: Truncates draft tree using offline-profiled verification cost; up to 2.35x over AR, 1.21x avg over EAGLE-3; works in SGLang.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not address batching or EP.
bearing: Threatens tree-pruning-by-expert-cost ideas

title: XShare: Collaborative in-Batch Expert Sharing for Faster MoE Inference
quote: cuts peak GPU load by up to 3x in expert-parallel deployments
proves: In-batch expert sharing reduces expert activation up to 30% under standard batching, cuts peak per-GPU load up to 3x under EP, and gives up to 14% throughput in speculative decoding.
does_not_prove: Approximates routing (changes expert choice); not acceptance-aware; DP placement of requests not addressed.
bearing: Threatens 'reduce EP peak load under spec decode' ideas; closest prior art for verify-induced EP skew

title: Tackling the Data-Parallel Load Balancing Bottleneck in LLM Serving: Practical Online Routing at Scale (BalanceRoute)
quote: every decode step ends in a synchronization barrier whose latency is set by the most heavily loaded worker.
proves: DP decode imbalance compounds step after step into wasted compute; BalanceRoute online routing reduces DP imbalance and improves throughput on 144 NPUs vs vLLM.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not mention speculative decoding or variable tokens per step; no numbers in abstract.
bearing: Supports: acceptance-aware DP routing is unaddressed by the main DP-balance paper

title: NanoCP: Request-Level Dynamic Context Parallelism for Data-Expert Parallel Decoding
quote: this binding cannot balance both simultaneously, producing EP stragglers
proves: Routing to DP instance with smallest KV makes batch sizes unequal and EP stragglers; request-level dynamic CP gives 1.88-3.27x higher request rate under TPOT SLO and 1.79-2.12x lower P99.
does_not_prove: No mention of speculative decoding or MTP on the abstract page.
bearing: Supports: DP-EP decode balancing is active research but spec-blind

title: Nightjar: Dynamic Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Large Language Models Serving
quote: up to 14.76% higher throughput than standard speculative decoding
proves: Bandit planner disables speculation when not beneficial and offloads the draft to CPU when GPU memory is tight to grow KV/batch; up to 14.76% throughput and 20.18% latency gain (v5, 2026-06). Earlier version claimed 27.29%.

does_not_prove: Attributed wording 'a single shared K' is not on the page (it says 'one shared K'). Close event has no linked commit, so 'completed' does not show per-request K landed in vLLM; maintainer objected to host-side verify_lens planning.
bearing: Threatens per-request K as novel; answered as direction in both engines.

title: SGLang issue #23705: [Roadmap] Adaptive Speculative Decoding Roadmap
quote: In fact, the main challenge for request-level policy is CUDA graph.
proves: Open roadmap; item 'Per-request/Mixed-workload policy: use accept-length distribution instead of only batch average' is unchecked; maintainer alphabetc1 says current design builds CUDA graphs per candidate step, which is not acceptable for request-level policy, needing piecewise CUDA graphs and kernel changes.
does_not_prove: No per-request policy implementation in this issue; DSpark ragged verify (K15) is a separate path.
bearing: Supports gap: per-request K under CUDA graphs is open in adaptive-spec path.

title: SGLang PR #28045: throughput-aware policy for cost-guided adaptive speculative steps
quote: that maximizes `score(S) = E[tokens | S steps] / cost_ms(batch_size, S)`
proves: Open, unmerged: profiles (batch_size, num_steps) -> latency at startup, tracks per-position acceptance in a sliding window shared across batch sizes, picks one step count per batch.
does_not_prove: Batch-level only, not per-request; not merged as of 2026-10-20.
bearing: Shows cost-aware batch K is in flight; per-request still absent.

title: SGLang PR #31716: spec-decoding context-aware adaptive routing
quote: This is evidence for exposing context as a policy input, not for a universal context-to-K default.
proves: Open, unmerged: adds optional (batch size, context bucket) slots; H100 BS=8 EAGLE3 Llama-3.1-8B: K=7 wins at ctx 256-4096, K=1 wins at 8192-16384 as acceptance falls to ~1.004.
does_not_prove: Still batch-level (bucketed), not per-request; single model/GPU.
bearing: Adds context length as K signal; batch granularity only.

title: DSpark in SGLang: Speculative Decoding with Confidence-Driven, Variable-Length Verification
quote: The scheduler is sizing each request, not applying one batch average.
proves: Confirmed: mixing gsm8k, arena-hard, poetry, mean verify window 5.24/3.78/2.91 tokens, utilization 0.88-0.97; ~55% of gsm8k steps fill the window of six, ~80% of poetry steps use three or fewer.
does_not_prove: DSpark-specific (confidence head); does not cover EAGLE/n-gram per-request K or tenant fairness.
bearing: Threatens per-request verify length as a gap: shipped in SGLang for DSpark.

title: llama.cpp issue #27852: ngram-cache speculative decoding keeps per-slot context cache across requests
quote: Suggested fix — reset the per-sequence state in `begin()`; `ngram_cache_dynamic`/`ngram_cache_static` are left alone since they are cross-request by design:
proves: Per-slot context carried across requests drops acceptance from 86% to 11% (41.5 to 19.4 t/s); resetting in begin() restores 86%. Dynamic/static n-gram caches are cross-request by design; a commenter notes such persistence makes results order-dependent.
does_not_prove: The 'cross-request by design' phrase applies to ngram_cache_dynamic/static, not to the per-slot bug; no tenant or privacy analysis.
bearing: Supports: cross-request drafter state causes interference between requests.

title: Red Hat CVE-2026-105752 (vLLM cache_salt not preserved on tool continuations)
quote: vLLM rebuilds the next-turn engine input without preserving the cache_salt value, so the continuation prefix is cached in the shared, unsalted namespace even when the caller enabled salting.
proves: Confirmed: /v1/responses Harmony tool continuations drop cache_salt; tenant can confirm prior prompts via cached-token counts; rated Low (CVSS 3.1 score 3.1); Red Hat fix deferred.
does_not_prove: Prefix cache only; page never mentions speculative decoding.
bearing: Shows salting is fragile in practice; analogy for drafter caches.

title: PrefixWall: Mitigating Prefix Caching Side Channels in Shared LLM Systems
quote: PrefixWall monitors cache reuse across users, flags suspicious sharing, and selectively isolates prefixes, restricting their reuse only when necessary.
proves: Selective isolation of APC prefixes gives up to 70% higher cache reuse and 30% lower latency vs per-user isolation.
does_not_prove: Abstract covers APC only; no speculative-decoding or drafter-cache defense seen.
bearing: Template for selective isolation; gap if applied to draft caches.

title: The Early Bird Catches the Leak: Unveiling Timing Side Channels in LLM Serving Systems
quote: we discovered a set of new timing side channels in LLM systems, arising from shared caches and GPU memory allocations, which can be exploited to infer both confidential system prompts and those issued by other users.
proves: Timing side channels on KV cache and semantic cache; token-by-token search recovers shared prompt prefixes; black-box tests on online services.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not cover speculative decoding.
bearing: Prior art for cache timing attacks; drafter channel not covered.

title: Time Will Tell: Timing Side Channels via Output Token Count in Large Language Models
quote: an adversary can recover the output token count reliably using a timing channel, even over the network against a popular closed-source commercial LLM.
proves: Output token count leaks target language (>75% precision) and input class (>70% precision, incl. GPT-4o); proposes tokenizer-, system-, prompt-based mitigations.
does_not_prove: Channel is output length, not speculation acceptance.
bearing: Adjacent channel; does not cover per-step acceptance leakage.

title: SuffixDecoding at Production Scale with Arctic Inference and vLLM (reopen L127)
quote: two key optimizations that now make it production-ready at all concurrency levels
proves: Confirmed wording; claims single configuration beats N-gram at all concurrency levels; 1.11x-1.17x over best N-gram on SpecBench, 1.02x-1.31x on BlazeEdit; custom hashmap 3.4x faster speculation.
does_not_prove: Vendor claim; no tenant isolation or adversarial analysis; compared against N-gram, not against no-spec at saturation (contrast K22).
bearing: Vendor framing; weakened by K22 saturation result.

title: vLLM RFC #51788: Suffix decoding on GPU (suffix_gpu) (reopen)
quote: Its aggregate advantage appears only as concurrency grows (AL 1.53 -> 2.33 from c1 to c256 at k=16, vs 1.98 -> 1.89 for the CPU tree), i.e. it comes from the cross-request global index compounding under concurrent traffic
proves: Confirmed: Llama-3.1-8B on L20, Spec-Bench; GPU global index AL 1.53 (c1) to 2.33 (c256); beyond ~c128 async no-spec beats every drafter (k=5 c256: 1654 vs 1467 tok/s).
does_not_prove: The CPU tree '1.98 -> 1.89' is c16 to c256, not c1 to c256: its own table shows suffix_sync k=16 at 1.54 (c1), 1.98 (c16), 1.89 (c256). Single GPU, single workload.
bearing: Supports: cross-request sharing drives suffix gains; spec loses at saturation.

title: ArcticInference cache.py SuffixDecodingCache.speculate (lines 288-308)
quote: draft = draft1 if draft1.score >= draft2.score else draft2
proves: Confirmed: draft1 comes from self._local_trees[req_id], draft2 from self._global_tree, both with same parameters; the local (per-request) draft wins ties.
does_not_prove: Does not show whether global tree is partitioned by tenant (it is one shared tree here).
bearing: Supports: global tree shared across requests with no tenant key.

title: vLLM v0.31.0 output_processor.py RequestOutputCollector (lines 51-77)
quote: When streaming deltas, RequestOutputs are merged if the producer gets ahead of the consumer.
proves: Confirmed: aggregate = (output_kind == DELTA); put() calls self.output.add(output, aggregate=self.aggregate) when an undelivered output exists, so a slow consumer receives merged deltas (multiple steps' tokens in one chunk).
does_not_prove: Merging depends on consumer speed, not a deliberate padding/aggregation policy; does not show the effect on network packet boundaries.
bearing: Natural partial aggregation; weakens clean per-step acceptance observation.
